Match grouped SReLU forward to the saved C precision while keeping activation math in FP32. No additional saved activation memory.

Includes regression tests, reference updates and documentation.

Companion TE PR: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3653

Pre-commit, syntax and whitespace checks passed. GPU tests remain pending. Please create as draft.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Grouped SReLU now applies activation to the pre-activation rounded to the output C tensor’s precision, keeping forward results consistent with backward recomputation. Activation arithmetic remains FP32.
  * Quantized outputs and their scales now match between forward evaluation and backward recomputation when inputs and quantization settings are the same.
* **Documentation**
  * Clarified the precision behavior and its impact on forward results.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `3064a43f9142` against base `e15aac24b52a`.

Thank you for your contribution! The saved-C rounding is in the right place: after alpha/bias and C storage, before either SReLU variant, with activation arithmetic retained in FP32. This aligns the forward activation input with backward recomputation without changing the saved tensor allocation. I found no actionable code defect in this bounded change. Matching probability and quantization inputs remains necessary, as documented. Native execution of the new precision and MXFP8 byte-equality tests is still pending. The merge-requirements check also needs a Project assignment; I filled the supported labels and milestone, but my token cannot access Projects.

Validation: Reviewed all five changed files and traced saved-C storage, alpha/bias ordering, scalar/vector activation arithmetic, backward recomputation, and row/column quantization inputs. Public forward compilation generates C; the new cast is conditional on the SReLU epilogue and C generation. Executed the actual new precision-test function against extracted old/new epilogue statements using CPU tensor adapters: old source fails all four BF16 cases while all four FP32 controls pass; new source passes all eight. This checks source semantics, not native CuTeDSL execution. Executed the actual changed reference on 40 CPU cases spanning FP32/BF16/FP16/E4M3/E5M2 C, plain/tanh-clamped activation, two groups, per-group alpha, optional bias, and per-row probabilities. Activation and amax agree with a separately assembled saved-C oracle; all eight FP32 controls remain unchanged. Ten reduced SM100 CuTeDSL compilation cases passed for the exact new tensor cast followed by packed FP32 squaring: five C dtypes with C generation enabled/disabled. No GPU was launched. All four changed Python files parse, and the head-to-base diff passes whitespace checks. Style and Docs workflows passed on this head.

Limitations: No native GPU execution, full grouped-kernel compilation, CUDA Graph replay, or GPU performance measurement was performed in this review. The four new forward/backward MXFP8 byte-equality cases remain unvalidated here; CPU adapters and reduced compilation do not establish their native result.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Completed review of `3064a43f9142` against `e15aac24b52a`. The saved-C precision fix works in native SM100 execution, but the new precision test has an unsupported input/output dtype combination (P2 inline). No P0 or high-risk P1 found. Posting a comment because an effective approval already exists.

Native validation on SM100, PyTorch 2.13/CUDA 13.0, cuDNN 9.27, CuTeDSL 4.7:
- The two new test functions produce **8 failed / 4 passed**: every saved-C precision case raises the D-dtype validation error before kernel execution; all four original MXFP8 forward/recomputation byte-and-scale equality cases pass.
- An isolated diagnostic preserves the precision assertions while using supported FP4 group32/E8M0 inputs and FP32 D, with packed ones (`0x22`). Together with the unchanged four MXFP8 cases, this gives **12 passed** on this head versus **8 failed / 4 passed** on its parent. The four parent FP32-C controls pass; the four BF16-C precision and four MXFP8 equality cases fail, establishing sensitivity to the fix. This diagnostic does not change the submitted tests.
- **20 existing tests passed**, covering discrete weights, raw-FP4 bias, scalar/vector tanh clamp, None-clamp identity, and clamp cache identity. All five changed files integrate cleanly with the reviewed base.

A bounded performance check used four groups of M=256, N=K=512, FP8 inputs, BF16 C/D and vector arithmetic. Base/head/head/base runs with preallocated execution and validated CUDA Graph replay measured GPU medians of **15.78 → 17.42 µs** for plain SReLU and **17.36 → 19.67 µs** for clamp=10 (approximately +10%/+13%). CPU enqueue medians stayed around 18 µs. These are two small workloads, not an application benchmark; the measured cost of the precision change should be considered when tuning the epilogue. Capture/replay and changed-probability replay matched the reference.

The existing CI request is pending evidence; no duplicate run was requested. Please repair the new precision-test configuration so native CI actually exercises its intended assertion. Validation here does not qualify other GPU architectures or TransformerEngine integration.

<!-- codex-fe-review:github-only:vedaanta:1501:3064a43f914215ce4a3c97618c15ef87eccc7d25:complete -->

[P2] Use a supported dtype combination in the precision regression test. This constructs FP8 A/B with FP32 D, but `GroupedGemmSreluSm100` explicitly rejects FP32 D for FP8 inputs. On SM100 all eight parametrizations fail with `ValueError: D dtype mismatch ... got Float32` before the kernel executes, so the new L0 test fails and never checks saved-C rounding. One verified way to retain the FP32-output oracle is FP4 inputs (`torch.uint8`) with group32/E8M0 scaling and packed-one initialization (`0x22` for A/B); that diagnostic passes all eight cases on this head, while the four BF16-C cases fail on the parent. Please use a supported configuration (or explicitly implement and validate the new dtype support). This is a nonblocking P2 under the review policy.

@@ -10,6 +10,14 @@ JAX arrays are **not supported**: both dense and discrete modes consume the SFA
 
 **Grouped GEMM + sReLU fusion**: A grouped block-scaled GEMM fused with a probability-gated squared-ReLU epilogue on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (SM100+), designed for MoE-style workloads. The API supports dense contiguous weights and discrete per-expert weight allocations. Groups are contiguous in the `M` dimension and described by `padded_offsets`.
 
+The pre-activation is rounded to the saved `C` tensor's dtype before evaluating
+plain or tanh-clamped squared-ReLU. With BF16 `C`, both the original forward and
+backward activation recomputation therefore consume `FP32(BF16(h_FP32))`.
+Activation arithmetic remains FP32. This changes forward numerics relative to
+applying the activation directly to the FP32 accumulator, but adds no saved
+activation memory. Matching probability inputs and quantization settings are
+also necessary for matching forward and recomputed quantized outputs.
+
 This kernel performs:
 1. **Block-scaled grouped GEMM** over contiguous expert ranges
 2. **sReLU epilogue** using per-row `prob`

+@pytest.mark.L0
+@torch_fork_set_rng(seed=0)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("c_dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("vector_f32", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tanh_clamp_scale", [None, 10.0])
+def test_grouped_gemm_srelu_uses_saved_c_precision(request, c_dtype, vector_f32, tanh_clamp_scale):
+    """Distinct FP32 accumulators in one BF16 bin must produce the same activation.
+
+    FP32 output exposes the activation input cast independently of output quantization.
+    FP32 C is a control: its distinct accumulator values must remain distinct.
+    """
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] != 10:
+        pytest.skip("Grouped SReLU requires SM100")
+    case = _build_srelu_case(request, torch.float8_e4m3fn, c_dtype, torch.float32, 32, torch.float8_e8m0fnu, vector_f32, False)
+    inputs, cfg = case
+    for name in ("a_tensor", "b_tensor", "sfa_tensor", "sfb_tensor"):
+        inputs[name].copy_(torch.ones_like(inputs[name], dtype=torch.float32))
+    inputs["prob_tensor"].fill_(0.5003)
+    outputs = []
+    for h in (1.0 + 1.0 / 1024, 1.0 + 3.0 / 1024):
+        inputs["alpha_tensor"].fill_(h / cfg["k"])
+        result = _run_srelu_case(case, tanh_clamp_scale=tanh_clamp_scale)
+        # Do not allow the test to pass by accidentally generating identical FP32 C.
+        expected_c = torch.full_like(result["c_tensor"], h)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(result["c_tensor"], expected_c, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        saved = result["c_tensor"].float()
+        if tanh_clamp_scale is None:
+            expected = saved.relu().square()
+        else:
+            expected = (tanh_clamp_scale * torch.tanh(saved.relu() / tanh_clamp_scale)).square()
+        expected = expected * inputs["prob_tensor"]
+        torch.testing.assert_close(result["d_tensor"], expected, rtol=2e-5, atol=2e-5)
+        outputs.append(result)
+    if c_dtype == torch.bfloat16:
+        assert torch.equal(outputs[0]["c_tensor"], outputs[1]["c_tensor"])
+        assert torch.equal(outputs[0]["d_tensor"], outputs[1]["d_tensor"])
+    else:
+        assert not torch.equal(outputs[0]["c_tensor"], outputs[1]["c_tensor"])
+        assert not torch.equal(outputs[0]["d_tensor"], outputs[1]["d_tensor"])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L0

+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] != 10:
+        pytest.skip("Grouped SReLU requires SM100")
+    case = _build_srelu_case(request, torch.float8_e4m3fn, c_dtype, torch.float32, 32, torch.float8_e8m0fnu, vector_f32, False)

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `3064a43f9142` against base `e15aac24b52a`.

Thank you for your contribution! The saved-C rounding is in the right place: after alpha/bias and C storage, before either SReLU variant, with activation arithmetic retained in FP32. This aligns the forward activation input with backward recomputation without changing the saved tensor allocation. I found no actionable code defect in this bounded change. Matching probability and quantization inputs remains necessary, as documented. Native execution of the new precision and MXFP8 byte-equality tests is still pending. The merge-requirements check also needs a Project assignment; I filled the supported labels and milestone, but my token cannot access Projects.

Validation: Reviewed all five changed files and traced saved-C storage, alpha/bias ordering, scalar/vector activation arithmetic, backward recomputation, and row/column quantization inputs. Public forward compilation generates C; the new cast is conditional on the SReLU epilogue and C generation. Executed the actual new precision-test function against extracted old/new epilogue statements using CPU tensor adapters: old source fails all four BF16 cases while all four FP32 controls pass; new source passes all eight. This checks source semantics, not native CuTeDSL execution. Executed the actual changed reference on 40 CPU cases spanning FP32/BF16/FP16/E4M3/E5M2 C, plain/tanh-clamped activation, two groups, per-group alpha, optional bias, and per-row probabilities. Activation and amax agree with a separately assembled saved-C oracle; all eight FP32 controls remain unchanged. Ten reduced SM100 CuTeDSL compilation cases passed for the exact new tensor cast followed by packed FP32 squaring: five C dtypes with C generation enabled/disabled. No GPU was launched. All four changed Python files parse, and the head-to-base diff passes whitespace checks. Style and Docs workflows passed on this head.

Limitations: No native GPU execution, full grouped-kernel compilation, CUDA Graph replay, or GPU performance measurement was performed in this review. The four new forward/backward MXFP8 byte-equality cases remain unvalidated here; CPU adapters and reduced compilation do not establish their native result.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.

Completed review of `3064a43f9142` against `e15aac24b52a`. The saved-C precision fix works in native SM100 execution, but the new precision test has an unsupported input/output dtype combination (P2 inline). No P0 or high-risk P1 found. Posting a comment because an effective approval already exists.

Native validation on SM100, PyTorch 2.13/CUDA 13.0, cuDNN 9.27, CuTeDSL 4.7:
- The two new test functions produce **8 failed / 4 passed**: every saved-C precision case raises the D-dtype validation error before kernel execution; all four original MXFP8 forward/recomputation byte-and-scale equality cases pass.
- An isolated diagnostic preserves the precision assertions while using supported FP4 group32/E8M0 inputs and FP32 D, with packed ones (`0x22`). Together with the unchanged four MXFP8 cases, this gives **12 passed** on this head versus **8 failed / 4 passed** on its parent. The four parent FP32-C controls pass; the four BF16-C precision and four MXFP8 equality cases fail, establishing sensitivity to the fix. This diagnostic does not change the submitted tests.
- **20 existing tests passed**, covering discrete weights, raw-FP4 bias, scalar/vector tanh clamp, None-clamp identity, and clamp cache identity. All five changed files integrate cleanly with the reviewed base.

A bounded performance check used four groups of M=256, N=K=512, FP8 inputs, BF16 C/D and vector arithmetic. Base/head/head/base runs with preallocated execution and validated CUDA Graph replay measured GPU medians of **15.78 → 17.42 µs** for plain SReLU and **17.36 → 19.67 µs** for clamp=10 (approximately +10%/+13%). CPU enqueue medians stayed around 18 µs. These are two small workloads, not an application benchmark; the measured cost of the precision change should be considered when tuning the epilogue. Capture/replay and changed-probability replay matched the reference.

The existing CI request is pending evidence; no duplicate run was requested. Please repair the new precision-test configuration so native CI actually exercises its intended assertion. Validation here does not qualify other GPU architectures or TransformerEngine integration.
